subject: Rivendell pilot: priority latency commitment request
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@rivendell.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Priority latency commitment for Rivendell pilot

David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a limited production pilot (US region) and procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a priority latency commitment for this pilot. High level ask: p95 <= 120ms for inference across the US region during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT), with a documented operational runbook for failover and fallback model variants.

Specific asks from our side:
- Confirm whether a p95 floor is feasible for our expected QPS (see attached expected_traffic)
- Outline telemetry you will expose (latency by route/model, region-level p95, error rates)
- Provide a short runbook for capacity failover and notification SLAs

I’ve attached the procurement request form (Rivendell_SLA_Request_20271120.pdf). Internal deadline: procurement review due 11/26.

Can your team confirm the above and tell us next steps/approx lead time for an approval path?

Best,
Alex Grant
Head of Platform
Rivendell AI
Attachments: Rivendell_SLA_Request_20271120.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@rivendell.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority latency commitment for Rivendell pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the procurement packet. I’ll route this through Product and Ops for a feasibility assessment and runbook draft. High-level next steps from our side:

1) Internal feasibility check (Product/Infra) — confirm p95 targets at QPS and burst levels
2) Telemetry matrix (what we expose via Console + token-level breakdowns)
3) Operational runbook (failover, model-variant fallback, notification path)
4) Draft commitment language for procurement to review — including carveouts for force majeure/region outages

Targeting to get an internal read and a first-pass runbook to you by EOD 11/24. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Priyom (Dedicated capacity/ops) to coordinate runbook + test plan.

David Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial_action_items.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:26:00 -08:00

On Sat, Nov 20, 2027 at 09:12 AM Alex Grant <alex.grant@rivendell.ai> wrote:
> David —
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a limited production pilot...

Quick internal note + questions from CS / Ops angle:

- Traffic profile: do we have an expected token/sequence length distribution? p95 is very sensitive to heavy-tail sequences (need sample prompts).
- Routing: will Rivendell accept routing to a cheaper compatible model during regional saturation, or do they need a hard guarantee on a specific model family?
- Warm KV cache / cold starts: need to know if they’ll run warmup traffic and what windows are critical (business hours only vs 24/7).
- Observability: propose exposing a dedicated token-level dashboard and an automated weekly latency digest during the pilot.
- Tests: we should run a staged load test against a dedicated pool to validate p95 at target QPS; I suggest we run an initial smoke test this week in a dev pool and a full run on 11/23.

I’ve attached an operational question list and a telemetry matrix to capture the above so we can hand to Product/Infra.

If Product confirms feasibility, we’ll need an Ops signoff on the runbook and a Dedicated capacity commit (Priyom).

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Attachments: operational_questions.docx, telemetry_matrix.xlsx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@rivendell.ai>, Procurement <procurement@rivendell.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority latency commitment for Rivendell pilot — internal runbook draft and tests

Alex / Procurement —

Appreciate the packet and the clear timeline. Quick status update and what we can commit to for the pilot: 

1) Feasibility: Product and Infra ran an initial validation against a dedicated dev pool. Results: p95 = 98ms at the sample QPS and sample prompt mix you provided; see attached latency-test-results.csv for the raw numbers.
2) Telemetry: We will expose a dedicated dashboard showing per-route p95, per-model p95, and 1-hour error rate summaries. Token-level cost breakdown will be available at token granularity in the Console.
3) Runbook: Draft attached (rivendell_runbook_v1.pdf). Key highlights: automated failover to a warm-compatible quantized model variant, alerting threshold at 250ms p95, and an initial notification SLA of 30 minutes for Sev-2 events during business hours.
4) Approval path: This is an exception to our standard hosted terms and requires an Ops/Dedicated capacity signoff (Priyom) and a final legal procurement redline. We’ll aim to provide the final commitment language for procurement by 11/26 to meet your internal deadline.

Pending items from your side: signed procurement acceptance of carveouts (force majeure, regional cloud outages) and confirmation whether warm-up windows will be run prior to go-live.

Next steps:
- Marissa / Priyom / Naomi and I will finalize the runbook and schedule a 60-minute walkthrough with your engineering team. Proposed slots: 11/25 10:00–11:00 PT or 11/26 09:00–10:00 PT.
- I’ll upload the formal commitment language to DocuSign once we have Ops signoff.

Thanks — we’re aligned to move this to pilot if procurement signs the carveout language.

David Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — david.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184
Attachments: rivendell_runbook_v1.pdf, latency-test-results.csv
